phase_0.boundary_condition: The closed set of three points defining a complete 3-uniform hypergraph

VINIT.justification: The state preceding the definition of the first point

AFWD.justification: The movement from point one to point two

AREV.justification: The return path to the origin point

CLINK.justification: The connection between vertices in the triad

IMSCRIB.justification: The point recognizing its own position in the set

FSPLIT.justification: The split into the second and third vertices

FFUSE.justification: The closure of the triangle back to the initial vertex

EVALT.justification: The successful completion of a valid edge

EVALF.justification: The absence of a valid edge

ENGAGR.justification: The state where the triangle is both open and closed

IFIX.justification: The permanent record of the hypergraph structure

phase_3.void_description: The empty set before the first vertex is placed
phase_3.true_description: The existence of a valid connection between vertices
phase_3.false_description: The absence of a connection between vertices
phase_3.both_description: The state of the hypergraph before the third vertex is fixed

steps.domain_action: Initialize the first vertex of the triad
Branch into the second and third vertex paths
Affirm the existence of the second vertex
Negate the path to the third vertex
Hold the triad in a state of potentiality
Reconstitute the triad into a single structure
Chain the vertices into a closed loop
Record the identity of the triad
Seal the system within the boundary

phase_5.memory_mechanism: The fixed record of the triad
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequential order of vertex placement

phase_6.cycle_cost: The energy required to define a vertex
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system is a closed logical structure where information is conserved through structural identity

composition_fingerprint.determines: the pair (ring_period_V, beta_max) is the machine-checkable fingerprint that separates this prime from every other; the flat 12-glyph crystal tuple does not
